item.title: Inokashira Park — Guide
item.description: Inokashira Park, in the fashionable suburb of Kichijoji in western Tokyo, is a beloved local park centred on a large, tree-fringed pond. A relaxed and lively place, it’s especially popular on weekends, with locals enjoying its natural setting, walking paths and easy-going atmosphere. The pond is famous for its swan-shaped pedal boats and rowing boats, a fun way to spend an afternoon on the water, and its cherry trees make it one of west Tokyo’s loveliest hanami spots in spring, their blossoms hanging over the water.

item.title: Ohori Park and Fukuoka Castle Ruins — Guide
item.description: Ohori Park is Fukuoka’s most beloved city park, built around a large pond created from the old moat of Fukuoka Castle. A scenic walking and jogging path circles the water, crossing a chain of small islands linked by stone bridges, with willows, pavilions and cafes along the way — a favourite spot for locals to stroll, relax and watch the sunset. Adjoining the park are the stone walls and ruins of Fukuoka Castle (Maizuru Park), once the largest castle in Kyushu, whose ramparts and turret sites give fine views and burst into cherry blossom in spring.

item.title: Shukkeien Garden: A Miniature Landscape in the City — Guide
item.description: Shukkeien, whose name means ‘shrunken-scenery garden’, is a beautiful traditional strolling garden in the middle of Hiroshima, laid out in 1620 for the local lord. As its name suggests, it miniaturises whole landscapes — mountains, valleys, forests and a central pond dotted with islets — into a compact space that unfolds scene by scene as you follow the path around the water. An arched rainbow bridge crosses the pond, tea houses sit among the maples and cherries, and carp fill the water.
